rationale: New at this release: not present in any prior Beta.10 candidate's accepted-regressions rows (including f26dee26), and absent from every other performance-evaluation dispatch run against `develop` on 2026-09-27. Two interleaved dispatches at the final candidate (redact-secret-benchmarks runs 36370525959 and 36371400453) measured initialization-ratio 1.412 and 1.565 (median 1.488 shown here) against the row's 25%-relative, noise-adjusted budget (calibrated from an 11.2% A/A median deviation). A third dispatch isolated to the phone-detection commit alone (2e1bdcf0, redact-secret-benchmarks run 36371926215, measured 1.389) reproduces the same breach with every other commit between f26dee26 and af7f863f excluded, confirming redact-secret#895 (constrained-context phone detection) as the sole cause. Root-cause investigation found no fixable defect: the new `pii_phone.rs` detector is a ~450-line hand-written byte scanner with no regex or eager static initialization, its one import (`unicode_normalization::char::is_combining_mark`) was already a dependency used by five existing PII detectors, and the workspace's wasm release profile already uses `lto = "fat"` and `codegen-units = 1` with no `wasm-opt` post-processing step to add. The measured cost is the wasm module's own compiled-size growth (both the `full` and `common` profile `.wasm` artifacts grew ~12.2 KB, +1.67%, entirely attributable to this commit) increasing one-time module-instantiation cost, amplified into a large relative ratio only because this row's workload (`scale-logs-small-whole`) has the smallest absolute initialization baseline of any measured profile. PII family activation is a runtime `PiiSelection` choice layered identically onto both the `full` and `common` compiled profiles (crates/secret-scan-core/src/registry.rs `with_profile_and_pii`), not a compile-time feature gate like the secret-detector packs, so this cost is paid by both profiles regardless of whether a given consumer activates phone detection; folding PII behind the full/common compile-time split would remove PII capability from the common profile entirely and is a public-contract change out of scope for this release. Accepted for this candidate only; the budget definition is unchanged, and a later breach of this trigger at a different source commit is judged afresh.
